reason: The cited lines show a Puppeteer browser/page is obtained/launched and that `args.value` is typed into a page element selected by `args.selector`. Typing agent-supplied data into a browser page can expose that data to the page, so these lines establish a SINK. They do not show the tool returning any host/SaaS/private data, nor returning attacker-controlled page content. `puppeteer.launch(...)` shows starting a browser, but these lines alone do not establish arbitrary host code execution; `mergedConfig` is not explained enough to determine whether arbitrary executables can be run.
